claim: Openia, the prior SOTA white-box method using only the last generated token's hidden state at the last layer, achieves 0.56-0.79 accuracy on independent-unit code correctness across DeepSeek-Coder, CodeLlama, and Magicoder under cross-benchmark and cross-task evaluation, far below the 0.987 AUROC benchmark from repeated sampling.
stance_target: single-pass hidden-state probing (even the field's prior SOTA) does not close the gap to sampling-based internal signal quality on standalone code
scope_conditions: HumanEval, MBPP independent-unit Python code; DeepSeek-Coder-1.3B/6.7B, CodeLlama-7B/13B, Magicoder-7B
quoted_support: This choice is motivated by the fact that the internal state from the last layer is closest to the model's final decision, making it a logical and effective representation for evaluating the correctness of the generated code.
numbers: Openia accuracy 0.56-0.79 across models and splits

claim: Middle transformer layers (layers 16-28 of 32) offer performance comparable to the last layer for code-correctness probing, and early-layer representations are highly sensitive to which token position is chosen while last-layer representations are robust to token choice -- motivating dynamic layer/token selection over Openia's fixed last-token/last-layer heuristic.
stance_target: the location of correctness-relevant internal signal within the network is not fixed and requires adaptive/dynamic selection strategies
scope_conditions: layer-wise ablation across DeepSeek-Coder, CodeLlama, Magicoder
quoted_support: peak performance is achieved with the representations from the last layer (layer 32), the middle layers (layers 16-28) still offer consistently strong results... representations from the last layer are more robust and less dependent on the specific token chosen.

claim: External LLM-as-Judge substantially outperforms both Openia's internal probing and black-box classifiers on independent-unit code correctness in most settings, reaching 0.75-0.97 accuracy, while In-house (self-judging) LLM-AJ performs poorly (0.27-0.68), indicating self-assessment overconfidence.
stance_target: the framing that no expressed interface communicates code correctness well -- an external verbalized judge is often the strongest single-pass signal for simple standalone code
scope_conditions: independent-unit HumanEval/MBPP code, cross-benchmark and cross-task splits
quoted_support: In practice, LLM-AJ requires no additional training but exhibits variable performance across settings, as shown by the drop in LLM-AJ's accuracy between the independent-unit and repo-level code generation scenarios.

claim: Training-set size shows diminishing returns for probe accuracy: accuracy/F1-Score climb from 0.71/0.67 with one training fold to 0.77/0.77 with three folds, then plateau with marginal gains beyond three folds.
stance_target: characterizes data efficiency of hidden-state probing classifiers, relevant to designing a single-GPU-feasible training pipeline
scope_conditions: probing classifier trained on MBPP internal representations
quoted_support: both accuracy and F1-Score rise as the training set increases from one to three folds, climbing from 0.71 (accuracy) and 0.67 (F1-score) at one fold to 0.77 for both metrics at three folds. Beyond three folds, performance gains plateau.
